title: Mobile Elevating Work Platforms
whatItIs: A MEWP, such as a scissor lift or a boom 'cherry picker', lifts people in a guarded platform. It prevents falls, but it can overturn, or throw out or trap the person in it.

keyFacts.text: A MEWP MUST be thoroughly examined at least every 6 months, or as an examination scheme sets.

keyFacts: Only trained operators who know that model should use it. The operator does the daily pre-use check.
Use it on firm, level ground; extend and chock any outriggers before raising the platform.
Boom MEWP with a fall risk: harness on a short restraint lanyard to the basket anchor.
Don't climb out of the basket at height or stand on the guard rails.
Have trained people on the ground who can lower the platform in an emergency.

visual.caption: Main MEWP dangers and how they're controlled (HSG150; HSE GEIS6)

items.title: Overturning
items.text: Firm, level ground; outriggers out; watch for trenches and manholes.

items.title: Being thrown out
items.text: Work-restraint harness in the basket. Don't overreach or stand on the guard rails.

items.title: Trapping and crushing
items.text: Take care near overhead structures: the controls can 'run on' briefly.

items.title: Overhead power lines
items.text: Don't operate close to overhead cables. Check the clearance before you start.

a.label: Scissor lift
points: Usually a bigger platform and more lift capacity

b.label: Boom ('cherry picker')
points: Risk of being thrown out if the boom jolts or tilts

onTheTest.question: Working from a boom MEWP, what personal fall protection does HSE prefer?
options: A harness on a short restraint lanyard clipped in the basket
A harness clipped to a nearby building
A harness with a long lanyard so you can reach
A life jacket at all times
onTheTest.why: GEIS6 and HSG150 para 177: work restraint, with a lanyard short enough to stop you reaching a fall position, fixed to an anchor in the basket.

onTheTest.question: Without an examination scheme, how often must a MEWP be thoroughly examined?
onTheTest.why: LOLER reg 9(3)(a): kit for lifting people, at least every 6 months (or per an examination scheme). 12 months is for other lifting kit.

traps: A MEWP isn't for getting off at height: leaving the basket needs a rigorous risk assessment first.
Never balance materials on the handrails, and never disable the overload system.
Don't drive with the platform raised unless the maker says it's designed for that.
Over water, if drowning is the bigger risk, wear a life jacket, not a harness.

sources.doc: HSE HSG150 Health and safety in construction
HSE GEIS6 The selection, management and use of MEWPs
